distinguishing_features: Physically modifies core architecture with a molded low-modulus polyurethane shell around the core rather than only changing a thermal setpoint trajectory

Introduces a compliant graded-density shell that redistributes binder-burnout stress by elastic strain-energy dissipation, not by inducing interfacial thermal stress from expansion mismatch to spall a deposit
Adds a silica buffer interface layer between foam shell and sand to manage thermal-gradient adhesion
Changes material composition/geometry of the core itself rather than operating an existing temperature-control loop
parsed.objective_technical_problem: How to prevent crack initiation at sharp geometric discontinuities in a foundry core caused by binder-burnout-induced stress without replacing the binder chemistry.
parsed.viable_reason: The proposed polyurethane foam shell would be destroyed by molten-metal pouring temperatures (far above its ~200°C limit) and the strain-energy arithmetic (31.25 kJ/m3) does not actually establish the claimed 10x margin or the 5 mm thickness, making the mechanism physically implausible and mis-derived as written.
parsed.non_obvious_reason: The compliant stress-dissipating shell geometry is a departure from the prior-art setpoint/monitoring approaches and is not an obvious routine extension of any of them, though it fails on viability grounds.
